limitations: The protocols remain separate. Their samples and medians are never pooled or averaged.
Protocol 1 recorded two slower large WASM cases, +10.8 percent and +18.6 percent. Protocol 2 does not prove what caused those regressions.
Protocol 2 amortizes scheduling slices across 32 calls and fixes CPU affinity. It also changes cache reuse and measurement duration. It does not represent one isolated model request.
The selected CPU was 36.7 percent busy in the preceding one-second sample. Pinning does not reserve an idle CPU or remove host contention.
The largest protocol 2 SIMD and base cases improved by only about 1.6 percent. These measurements do not establish a broad margin or a universal fastest implementation.
The helper compares the prior scalar formula and optimized Store::row within one candidate-linked instance. It does not time two separately built complete runtimes.
Complete-request controls remain small and mixed. They do not establish a whole-model or catalog-wide speedup.
Kev exports raw distributions. Laya exports rounded public noul. Zero Laya delta applies to the recorded public value, not unexported logits.
Request time medians and median paired ratios use different aggregation. The displayed medians need not imply the displayed paired change.
Native helper parity is checked before timing. WASM helper parity is also checked after every timed pair.
Both exact helper source versions, all raw receipts, the original nine archives and the first report are retained. Store and dequantization math did not change between protocols.
Archives contain scientific results, text sources and hashes. They contain no weights, helper binaries or runtime WASM bytes.
